symptom: `diff-local --ref HEAD~1..HEAD` after a unit's .mxunit moved to another name (another unit ID) printed `Warning: failed to read HEAD version of mprcontents/<old>.mxunit: exit status 128` and `Summary: 0 new, 0 modified, 0 deleted` — the change counted nowhere
cause: `git diff --name-status` detects renames by default (diff.renames), and reported the move as `R100\told\tnew`; findChangedMxunitFiles took the second field (the OLD path) and a status that is neither A nor D, so the unit was read as modified at a path the new revision does not have
insight: An .mxunit's file name IS its unit ID, so a git 'rename' is never a rename to Mendix — it is one unit deleted and another added, and that is what diff-local must report. Git's similarity detection makes this reachable without anyone moving a file: a document duplicated and the original deleted can pair up as R<similarity>. Ask git for exactly the semantics you parse (--no-renames) instead of parsing a format with optional third fields. Real-git test: `git mv` a unit to a new UUID name, commit, diff HEAD~1..HEAD → want 1 new, 1 deleted.
